definition.name: The Reluctant One — becoming what you refuse to believe you are
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Identity — Who am I, really? A name is stripped off one man and pressed onto him; the plot tracks whether he accepts it by faith before he can embody it.
definition.summary: A voice names Neo 'the One' and demands a 'Yes' before he has grounds to accept it (ev-008), but he spends the story rejecting the title — denying he is the One even as he commits to a rescue (ev-032). Only after death and revival does he seize the identity, halting bullets and reading the room as code (ev-045). The arc suspends the label between destiny and self-authorship until the final choice makes it real.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's opening move: a voice names Neo 'the One' and demands a 'Yes' before he has any grounds to accept it (ev-008). It installs the withheld label and the demand for faith that the whole arc will resolve.
chain.caused_by_previous: First link in the chain. The reclaiming/implant-extraction sequence delivers Neo into the car where the naming-and-demand occurs; nothing prior in THIS chain sets it up, so it is the seed event.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus reframes the rescue as destiny by recounting the myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy, then declares 'the search is over.' This is the external destiny-pressure that pins the 'One' name onto Neo — the identity he will keep refusing.
chain.caused_by_previous: Having been named 'the One' and brought into the real world (ev-008 → ev-010 → ev-013), Neo is now recovered and spent, which is the condition Morpheus uses to install the prophetic identity as the story's central burden.

chain.why_in_plot: The sparring test targets Neo's self-conception directly: he comes out of the download 'convinced he now knows how to fight,' and Morpheus refuses to celebrate the claim, dismantling it. This is the plot's 'who am I, really?' question applied to ability vs. identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's 'search is over' declaration (ev-014) commits him to guide Neo into training, so the download-and-test becomes the first proving of whether the named One can embody what he's told he is.

chain.why_in_plot: The rooftop jump makes the mind-over-physics test explicit and Neo 'runs and falls badly short' — a visible failure to become what he's been told he is. It keeps the label suspended between destiny and self-authorship.
chain.caused_by_previous: The dismantling of his technique-driven confidence in the spar (ev-015) leads to the harder test of belief itself: if he cannot accept he is the One, he cannot leap.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count ('five before him took on an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing'), and 'Neo takes it as caution and retreats toward the ladder, shaken rather than converted.' This directly pressures the faith-vs-evidence dilemma at the heart of the
chain.caused_by_previous: The jump's failure (ev-016) and the crew's split between doubters and believers leave Neo vulnerable to the argument that belief in the One is a lethal delusion — the caution he internalizes here.

chain.why_in_plot: At the Oracle's threshold Neo 'backs away before committing,' and he presses Morpheus over the five failed candidates — the direct echo of the prophecy's cost. His hesitation is the refusal-to-believe-he-is-the-One made spatial.
chain.caused_by_previous: Cypher's 'shaken rather than converted' warning (ev-020) primes Neo to interrogate the prophecy on the way in, turning the approach to the Oracle into a test of whether he can accept the named identity.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo leaves the Oracle 'carrying a private verdict and a death-prophecy he is ordered to keep' — the sealed, unaccepted verdict on his identity that will govern his choices until the climax.
chain.caused_by_previous: The threshold-backing and questioning (ev-022) resolve into a private audience whose verdict Neo cannot yet own, so the prophecy becomes a hidden weight rather than an embraced identity.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's explicit midpoint of refusal: 'He denies being the One, so his mission becomes a wager on a man rather than a prophecy — something he cannot justify logically, only believe in.' He commits to a rescue while rejecting the title — faith without identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: The Oracle's death-prophecy and Morpheus's imminent breaking under doubled serum (ev-023 → ev-031) force the choice; Neo answers it with action while still denying the name, which is exactly the suspended state the plot tracks.

chain.why_in_plot: In the rescue's aftermath, 'Neo tries to report what the Oracle told him, but Morpheus cuts him off and reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation.' The crew keeps pressing the named identity onto him even as he withholds assent.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's self-denying rescue (ev-032) succeeds spectacularly, which the believers read as proof of the One — tightening the gap between what he did and what he will admit he is.

chain.why_in_plot: Trapped and told to run, 'Neo does not run. He turns back... and hardens into a fixed, gunfighter's calm,' and 'Morpheus reads that stillness as the beginning of belief.' This is the first visible turn from refusal toward embodied identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: The failed extraction and Smith's point-blank trap (ev-037) leave Neo alone with the hunter; the pressure that began with the naming (ev-008) and the denied title (ev-032) now forces a stance instead of a flight.

chain.why_in_plot: At the edge of death 'Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces' and 'summons an impossible surge' — he begins to embody the One while still verbally refusing it, the tension the plot suspends right up to the end.
chain.caused_by_previous: The decision to stand and fight rather than run (ev-038) converts stillness into action; the refusal of Smith's pronouncement is the same refusal of the label, now expressed as power he cannot yet name.

chain.why_in_plot: The death-and-revival pivot: Neo is shot dead and confirmed gone, then Trinity's refusal and kiss bring the monitors 'jump back to life.' This is the necessary annihilation of the old, label-refusing self before he can seize the identity.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's stand and surge against Smith (ev-039) funnel him into the dead-end flight (ev-041 → ev-043) where Smith's point-blank shot completes the fate Neo refused — death — which the plot requires before rebirth.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's resolution: 'Only after death and revival does he seize the identity, halting bullets and reading the room as code.' Revived, Neo halts the Agents' volley, reads the room as flowing code, and destroys Smith — he finally embodies the named One.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's death and revival (ev-044) remove the last barrier to acceptance; the faith that began as a demanded 'Yes' (ev-008) and a wager on a man (ev-032) is now made real by his own choice, so Morpheus can declare him the One.

definition.name: The Rescue — going back in for a man you cannot save by logic
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Morpheus models the sacrifice horn by giving his life so Neo can escape (ev-025), and is then captured and broken by the Agents (ev-031). Neo stops Morpheus's plug from being pulled and commits to going back in, denying he is the One so the mission becomes a wager on a man rather than a prophecy (ev-032). He then storms the building, pulls Morpheus from a mid-dive gunshot (ev-034), and the crew's belief in him crystallizes in the aftermath (ev-035).

chain.why_in_plot: It is the plot's first sacrifice beat: Morpheus 'choos[es] to give his own life so the others can escape,' the act of self-sacrifice that the plot's dilemma (self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice) is built on and that Neo will later answer by going back.
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the chain's starting event. The Agents and cops converging on the crew's hiding place in the wall erupt into a firefight, and an Agent ambushing Neo is what forces Morpheus to burst through, pin the Agent, and order Trinity to get Neo out — i.e., to give his life.

chain.why_in_plot: It delivers the plot's central loss: Morpheus is captured (and about to be 'broken by the Agents'), the consequence of the sacrifice in ev-025 that turns him into the man who must be rescued.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's self-sacrifice in the wall (ev-025) leaves him fighting the Agents alone upstairs in Room 808 while the others descend; his isolation is what lets the Agents take him into custody.

chain.why_in_plot: It shows the man being 'broken' — Smith escalates to 'a doubled serum dosage' that drives Morpheus toward breaking — which is exactly the 'man you cannot save by logic' the plot names and the pressure that makes Neo's rescue a wager rather than a calculation.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's capture (ev-026) is what puts him in the executive office in Smith's hands, where the interrogation and serum can be applied.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the plot's decisive turn — Neo 'stops the plug from being pulled' and 'commits to going back,' explicitly reframing the mission as 'a wager on a man rather than a prophecy' that 'he cannot justify logically,' which is the plot's own definition.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus being broken and about to give up Zion's codes (ev-031) is what triggers the crew to reach for the plug, and what Neo stops — converting the sacrifice into a rescue.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the rescue itself: Neo 'storms the building, pulls Morpheus from a mid-dive gunshot,' the physical payoff of the commitment made in ev-032.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's decision to go back (ev-032) is what enables the crew to launch, Neo to drop the helicopter into the office, extract Morpheus by force, and leap after him when Smith shoots him mid-dive.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the plot's resolution beat: 'the crew's belief in him crystallizes in the aftermath,' the thematic reward for choosing the man over the prophecy.
chain.caused_by_previous: The successful rescue (ev-034) is what allows the aftermath on the roof, where Tank's watch 'resolves into certainty' and Morpheus reinterprets the prophecy around the man he just saved.

definition.name: The Awakening to the Real — swallowing the truth that unmakes a comfortable life
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Truth vs. a comfortable lie — is it better to know an unbearable reality or live a pleasant illusion?
definition.summary: Morpheus recasts Neo's lifelong dread as an enslaving system and offers a choice between forgetting and knowing; Neo takes the red pill (ev-010). He is then born into the real world (ev-011) and recoils as he learns the world is a simulation and humans are farmed for power — the truth as an unbearable violation (ev-013). The plot prices honesty as a loss that cannot be un-known.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's ignition: an unseen party contacts Neo through his own machine and tells him to 'follow a white rabbit,' pulling him toward the truth he has always sensed. It reframes his 'lifelong dread' (the plot's core subject) as something real and reachable, setting up the choice to come.
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the first link. It is set in motion by the unseen party typing on Neo's machine and issuing the 'follow a white rabbit' instruction, which draws Neo out of his ordinary life toward the source of the truth.

chain.why_in_plot: The abstract pull becomes an active summons: Morpheus's voice guides Neo out of the office while 'forces are closing in,' physically moving him toward the truth and forcing him toward a threshold (the ledge) he cannot yet cross. The comfortable life is now actively collapsing under the pressure of a
chain.caused_by_previous: The contact begun in ev-004 escalates into a real raid: the ringing phone delivers Morpheus's warning that 'forces are closing in,' turning Neo's drawn-out curiosity into a guided, urgent flight toward the truth.

chain.why_in_plot: The system retaliates against Neo's movement toward knowing: the Agents seize and interrogate him, and Smith offers to 'wipe his record clean' (the comfortable lie) in exchange for Morpheus. Neo's refusal and the physical silencing of his mouth mark the cost of choosing the truth over a restored, un
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's failure to cross the ledge in ev-006 leaves him trapped at the base of the skyscraper, so the Agents close in and capture him, converting his stalled escape into an interrogation.

chain.why_in_plot: Having refused the wipe, Neo is extracted from the lie and delivered to the one who 'knows everything.' A voice names him 'the One' and demands a single 'Yes' — the prelude to the choice — while the implanted tracker (the system's grip) is still inside him, so the movement toward knowing is now ir
chain.caused_by_previous: The implanted creature burrowing inside Neo at the end of ev-007 is what the rescuers must counter; the ringing phone and the voice demanding 'Yes' reclaim him from the Agents' custody and carry him toward Morpheus.

chain.why_in_plot: Before Neo can be offered the truth, the system's physical hold must be removed: Trinity extracts the implanted tracker, which reverts to a common wire tap — exposing the surveillance that maintained his comfortable illusion. This clears the way for the choice itself.
chain.caused_by_previous: The tracker implanted in ev-007 and still burrowing in ev-008 is now forcibly removed by Trinity's extractor and electric charge, freeing Neo from the Agents' tracking so he can be taken to Morpheus.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's central decision. Morpheus 'reframes Neo's lifelong, nameless dread as a real enslaving system and offers him a choice between forgetting and knowing,' and Neo swallows the red pill — directly enacting the theme 'is it better to know an unbearable reality or live a pleasant ill
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's reclamation and 'Yes' in ev-008 (and the removal of the tracker in ev-009) deliver him to Morpheus, who now presents the explicit choice between the blue pill (forgetting) and the red pill (knowing) that Neo accepts.

chain.why_in_plot: The choice's consequence: Neo is 'born into the real world,' physically ejected from the pod. This is the irreversible step — the comfortable life is literally shed as he enters reality, the first price of the truth paid in flesh.
chain.caused_by_previous: Swallowing the red pill in ev-010 liquefies Neo's reality (the mirror crawls into him) and triggers the trace; his body goes into cardiac arrest and ruptures the amnion, so he is flushed into the waste line and born into the real world.

chain.why_in_plot: The aftermath of birth: Neo is rebuilt and Morpheus begins 'dismantling his assumptions about himself and his era,' leading him 'to witness the reality rather than describe it.' This is the deliberate, guided confrontation with the truth that the plot prices as a loss.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's near-drowning and rescue from the sewer in ev-011 leave him recovered aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, where Morpheus — 'certain they have found the one' — rebuilds his atrophied body and prepares to show him the truth.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's emotional and thematic payoff: Morpheus walks Neo through 'the truth of the Matrix' — that the world is a simulation and humans are 'farmed for power.' Neo 'recoils' and experiences the truth as 'an unbearable violation,' exactly matching the plot's framing of knowledge as a
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's dismantling of Neo's assumptions in ev-012 leads directly to jacking him into the Construct, where Morpheus reveals the full truth of the Matrix and Neo's mind and body rebel against what cannot be un-known.

definition.name: The Betrayer — trading a hard, meaningful freedom for a soft, empty comfort
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Meaning vs. pleasure — a life of purposeful struggle or empty satisfaction?
definition.summary: Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' (ev-020) and bargains with the Agents, savoring a fabricated steak while choosing to be re-plugged into the lie. His treachery turns open aboard the ship: he murders Apoc and Switch, delivers Morpheus to the Agents, and is struck down by Tank, who survived (ev-029). The arc is the counter-argument to Neo's route made flesh — purpose chosen over pleasure.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's thesis is Cypher choosing soft, empty comfort over hard freedom; this is where it is forged. He recasts Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' (the text's ev-020 anchor) to justify his disillusionment, then savors a fabricated steak and strikes a bargain with an Agent — the exact 'trading'
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the first link; it sets the chain moving. His ideological rejection of the struggle (the prophecy as body count) and his taste of the simulated steak motivate him to seek a way back into the lie.

chain.why_in_plot: The bargain made in ev-020 must be operationalized; here Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can during the crew's trip to the Oracle — the act of a man who has already defected, enabling the Agents to track them
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by the deal struck in ev-020: having bargained with the Agent, Cypher now plants the beacon that will let the trap close.

chain.why_in_plot: The betrayal's payoff: the Matrix is rewritten around the crew, Mouse is killed, and the group is sealed in — the 'body count' Cypher predicted begins, and Morpheus is forced into the traceable phone that makes his capture possible
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Cypher's planted beacon in ev-021, which exposes and rewrites the Matrix around the crew, springing the trap.

chain.why_in_plot: The cascade of Morpheus's capture runs through this: the Agents converge because the trap (ev-023) worked, and Morpheus chooses to sacrifice himself so Neo can escape — the hard, meaningful struggle that Cypher's route rejects
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the trap closing in ev-023, which drives the crew into the wall and brings the Agents down on their hiding place.

chain.why_in_plot: The culmination of the betrayal's design: Morpheus is captured. Cypher is present in the basement sequence, and his treachery is what delivered Morpheus into the Agents' hands
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by the converging Agents in ev-025, which forces the crew down into the basement where Morpheus is overwhelmed and taken.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher reaches the exit first and wakes aboard the ship to draw a concealed rifle — the betrayer returning to the real world not to fight machines but to murder his crew, the open turn of his treachery
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by his earlier covert deal (ev-020) and beacon (ev-021): he is routed to the exit ahead of the others so he can strike aboard the ship.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's central event made explicit: Cypher murders Apoc and Switch, delivers Morpheus to the Agents, and is struck down by Tank, who survived (the text's ev-029 anchor). This is the treachery 'turned open aboard the ship'
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by Cypher waking armed at the exit in ev-028: once the survivors jack back in, he executes the murders his concealed rifle promised.

definition.name: The Hunter and the Chosen — a program enforcing fate against a man who overrides it
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Freedom vs. determinism — do we choose, or is the path already written?
definition.summary: The prophecy of the One and the Oracle's verdict set a pre-scripted world (ev-014, ev-023), while Agent Smith moves to enforce it, framing Neo's death as settled inevitability at the third-rail (ev-039). At the edge of death Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces, summons an impossible surge, and breaks free (ev-039). The plot's loudest claim is that choice overrides destiny — Neo then enters and destroys Smith, the first Agent ever killed (ev-045).

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's thesis statement: Morpheus reframes the rescue as destiny via the Oracle's prophecy of the One, establishing the pre-scripted world the plot opposes.
chain.caused_by_previous: First link — sets the chain moving (Neo's rescue and recovery create the moment for Morpheus to impose the prophecy).

chain.why_in_plot: Neo carries away a private 'death-prophecy' verdict from the Oracle — the second pillar of the pre-scripted world (the Oracle's verdict) that the plot names as setting fate.
chain.caused_by_previous: The prophecy's claim (ev-014) is actualized when Neo receives the Oracle's verdict, personalizing the written path he will later refuse.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's pivot: Smith uses the train to frame Neo's death as settled inevitability, and Neo refuses the name/fate Smith pronounces, summoning an impossible surge to break free — choice overriding destiny.
chain.caused_by_previous: The death-prophecy verdict (ev-023) returns as Smith enforcing that exact 'settled inevitability,' provoking Neo's refusal of the written fate.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's loudest claim realized: Neo enters and destroys Smith, the first Agent ever killed — choice literally destroying the enforcer of fate.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's surge that broke the framed death (ev-039) carries directly into him turning on Smith and destroying the Agent.
